one_liner: Rust RFC 5322/MIME e-mail parser with SIMD scanning and lazy zero-copy decoding; 9x to 31x GMime, VMime, libEtPan!, Dovecot.
what_it_does: Parses a whole raw message (RFC 5322, MIME RFC 2045-2049, RFC 2047/2231 and many mail RFCs) from a byte slice into a read-only Message that is read through Copy views: typed header getters (subject(), from(), date(), message_id(), received()), the MIME part tree, nested message/rfc822 parts and the RFC 8621 text/HTML/attachment body lists. Bodies are transfer-decoded and charset-converted only when read (text(), decoded(), text_prefix()), across 41 charsets, with Shift_JIS, Big5, GB18030 and other multi-byte CJK charsets behind the optional full_encoding feature (encoding_rs). It cannot build or modify messages (separate mail-builder crate) and has no C API, so it is not a drop-in for GMime, VMime, libEtPan! or Dovecot lib-mail.
how_it_is_fast: SIMD kernels (NEON on aarch64, AVX2 and SSE2 on x86-64, memchr elsewhere) find MIME boundaries and header-field ends; header names, charset labels and HTML entities are looked up with compile-time perfect hashing (the hashify crate); a message is stored in a handful of flat vectors and strings borrow from the input (zero-copy). Nothing is decoded during parse; when a body is read, Base64 and quoted-printable go through encodify's SIMD codecs and UTF-8 is validated with simdutf8. parse_with() plus MessageBuffers reuses one message's storage for the next.
when_to_use: Rust mail servers, indexers, spam or DKIM pipelines that parse many messages but read few bodies: on the author's Apple M4 the headers workload runs 2,638 MiB/s on Enron (Dovecot 480, libEtPan! 266, VMime 137, GMime 132).
Full decoding of ordinary mail: Enron full workload 2,420 MiB/s vs Dovecot 366, libEtPan! 96, VMime 70 and GMime 65; attachment-heavy messages 12.7 GB/s vs GMime 960 MiB/s.
JMAP or IMAP servers that need RFC 8621 body lists, has_attachments(), part roles and decode-problem flags (isEncodingProblem) rather than raw MIME trees.
Untrusted input: the parser has nesting, part-count and encoded-nesting limits (64, 10,000 and 3 by default), cargo-fuzz targets for parser, fields, charsets, kernels and mbox, and Miri test runs.
when_not_to_use: C or C++ code bases: Rust only, so you need your own FFI layer; the 1.0 line requires Rust 1.98, a very recent toolchain.

You need a released, stable API today: the benchmarked 1.0.0 is an unreleased breaking rewrite; crates.io still serves 0.11.9 (2026-09-09), which decodes every body during parse, has a different API and is not in the published tables.
Streaming or very large inputs: parse() takes the whole message as one slice and returns None for input of 4 GiB or more; Dovecot's istream-based message-parser works block by block.
Building, editing or re-serialising messages: the parsed message is read-only (use mail-builder).
Legacy CJK mail without the full_encoding feature: those bodies are decoded as UTF-8 and reported as an unknown charset.

integration.dependencies: hashify 0.3, memchr 2.8, simdutf8 0.1, encodify 1.0; optional encoding_rs 0.8 (full_encoding) and serde
integration.min_toolchain: Rust 1.98 for 1.0.0 (repository; edition 2024); 0.11.9 on crates.io has no declared MSRV
integration.platforms: any Rust target; SIMD kernels on aarch64 (NEON) and x86-64 (AVX2 and SSE2), memchr fallback elsewhere; only Apple silicon macOS was benchmarked
integration.thread_safety: MessageParser, Message and the views are Send + Sync (README and CHANGELOG); build one parser and share it; parse_owned() gives a Message<'static> that can move between threads

gotchas: Harness asymmetry in the full workload: the GMime shim calls g_mime_text_part_get_text, which in GMime 3.2.15 opens an iconv filter whenever a charset parameter is present, UTF-8 to UTF-8 included (gmime-text-part.c lines 280-288, no same-charset shortcut in g_mime_filter_charset_new), while the VMime and libEtPan! shims skip conversion for UTF-8 bodies and only run g_utf8_validate_len. So GMime's 1 MB UTF-8 body goes through macOS iconv at 97 MiB/s against 2,212 (VMime) and 2,796 (libEtPan!), which is the 176.61x top of the README's '13 to 177' range; without that corpus the GMime full geometric mean is about 23x rather than 31x (derived from page data in results/summary.md). It is GMime's ordinary API, but the shims are not tuned equally.

The headers and structure ratios measure header parsing plus boundary scanning only: no library decodes bodies there, throughput is corpus bytes over time, so corpora with large bodies reach 80,868 MiB/s and the 1 MB plain-text cells hundreds of GB/s; the README excludes plain-large from those geometric means but not from the full one.

The numbers were measured on 2026-09-28 at the 1.0.0 merge; later commits (SSSE3 tier, charset label remapping, an address-lexer fix for backslash escapes #162, HTML text fixes) were not re-measured. Only one machine was used (Apple M4, NEON path); the AVX2/SSE2 kernels, Linux, glibc iconv and distribution GLib were not measured, and GMime and VMime copy the input into their own streams as their users would.

unsafe is confined to the SIMD kernels and a UTF-8 module that turns already-validated bytes into str/String; Miri cannot run every NEON instruction encodify uses, so the parser's Miri runs use encodify's portable path (--cfg encodify_scalar, which only works from encodify 1.0.1).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: No other e-mail parser is catalogued; encodify (its Base64/quoted-printable layer) is the sibling to take when you only need transfer encodings without MIME parsing. Against the most used Rust parser, mailparse 0.17.0 (not catalogued), mail-parser is 1.3x to 4.6x faster on the full workload of the README corpora (3.0x geometric mean; 1.25x on the 1 MB plain-text body) and also handles boundary-prefix lines correctly where mailparse splits them.
verified_claims_summary: On an Apple M4 Mac mini (macOS 26.6.2), mail-parser 1.0.0 built by rustc 1.98.1 (release, opt-level 3) was timed with criterion against GMime 3.2.15, VMime master 5b01911, libEtPan! 1.10.1 and Dovecot 2.4.5 lib-mail, all built from pinned sources at -O3 with Apple clang 21 and driven through project-written C/C++ shims, median of three runs over 11 corpora: full-workload geometric means of 31x GMime, 20x VMime, 15x libEtPan!, 9.3x Dovecot and 3.0x mailparse, headers 5.2x to 33x, with a published equivalence check showing equal message, part and leaf counts on Enron and the generated corpora.
status_note: Actively maintained (last commit 2026-10-10, about 4.25 million crates.io downloads, the parser of Stalwart Mail Server, Apache-2.0 OR MIT, copyable), but the measured 1.0.0 rewrite is unreleased and needs Rust 1.98; tier A harness whose GMime column pays a UTF-8-to-UTF-8 iconv pass the other C shims skip.
